title: Creamy Persimmon Sorbet with Black Tea
changes_from_base: Ripe persimmon blended with sugar and loosened with cold black tea replaces the mango and lime; no corn syrup, no cooked syrup.
summary: Very ripe persimmons blend into a naturally creamy purée; a splash of strong black tea adds depth and a gentle tannic edge.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Tea
steps.text: Pour 150 ml boiling water over 2 black teabags, leave for 5 min, squeeze them out, then measure 120 ml and let it cool.

steps.title: Prepare the fruit
steps.text: Pull off the persimmon leaves, peel the fruit with a small knife and chop the flesh, discarding any seeds.

steps.title: Purée
steps.text: Blend the flesh with the sugar on high for about 30 seconds, until completely smooth and glossy.

steps.title: Strain and season
steps.text: Sieve the purée, measure 500 ml into the jug and whisk in the tea, lemon juice and salt. Taste and adjust the lemon.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Put the jug in the freezer for 2-3 h, stirring once, until icy cold.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Churn for 20-25 min, then freeze for 4 h for a firmer scoop.

tips: Use persimmons so soft they feel like water balloons; firm ones taste chalky.
Any leftover purée is lovely stirred into yoghurt.
Swap the tea for water if you prefer a pure fruit flavour.
storage: Keep covered in the freezer for up to 1 week; sorbet turns icy after that. Soften for 10 min before scooping.
